accepted.question_text: Let f(n) be the maximum number of edges in a graph on n vertices in which no two cycles have the same length. Is it true that the asymptotic normalized gap between f(n) and n satisfies lim_{n→∞} (f(n) − n)/√n = √2.4?
accepted.context_brief: Asymptotic growth of graphs with distinct cycle lengths.

accepted.question_text: Let f(n) be the maximum number of edges in a graph on n vertices in which no two cycles have the same length. Does the lower asymptotic normalized gap satisfy lim inf_{n→∞} (f(n) − n)/√n ≤ √3?
accepted.context_brief: Weaker asymptotic bound for distinct-cycle-length graphs.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1.5 (Lai[30]) lim inf n→∞ f(n) − n / √n ≤ √3.

accepted.question_text: Let f(n) be the maximum number of edges in a graph on n vertices in which no two cycles have the same length. Does the lower asymptotic normalized gap satisfy lim inf_{n→∞} (f(n) − n)/√n ≤ √2.4?
accepted.context_brief: Sharper weaker asymptotic bound for distinct-cycle-length graphs.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1.6 (Lai[31]) lim inf n→∞ f(n) − n / √n ≤ √2.4.

accepted.question_text: Let f2(n) be the maximum number of edges in a 2-connected graph on n vertices in which no two cycles have the same length. Is it true that lim_{n→∞} (f2(n) − n)/√n = 1?
accepted.context_brief: Asymptotic 2-connected version of the distinct cycle-length problem.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1.11 ( Boros, Caro, Füredi and Yuster [3]) lim f2(n) − n / √n = 1.

accepted.question_text: Among hamiltonian graphs on n vertices in which no two cycles have the same length, what is the maximum possible number of edges?
accepted.context_brief: Hamiltonian graphs with all cycle lengths distinct.

evidence.quote: Problem 1.12 (Markström [27]) Determine the maximum number of edges in a hamiltonian graph on n vertices with no repeated cycle lengths.

accepted.question_text: Let g(n) denote the least number of edges of a graph that contains a cycle of length k for every integer 1 ≤ k ≤ n. Is it true that g(n) = n + log2 n + O(1) as n → ∞?
accepted.context_brief: Edge-minimal graphs containing every cycle length up to n.

evidence.quote: Let g(n) denote the least number of edges of a graph which contains a cycle of length k for every 1 ≤ k ≤ n.
Conjecture 1.16 (Jia[25]) g(n) = n + log2 n + O(1), as n → ∞.

accepted.question_text: Fix nonnegative integers a1, a2, …, an. For a graph G of order n, let ci denote the number of cycles of length i in G, and let f(a1, a2, …, an) be the maximum possible number of edges in a graph satisfying ci ≤ ai for every i. Determine f(a1, a2, …, an) for the general cycle-length distribution constraint problem.
accepted.context_brief: Generalized extremal problem with prescribed upper bounds on cycle counts.

evidence.quote: Let f(a1, a2, · · · , an) denote the maximum possible number of edges in a graph which satisfies ci ≤ ai where ai is a nonnegative integer.
Shi posed the problem of determining f(a1, a2, · · · , an) which extended the problem due to Erdös, it is clearly that f(n) = f(1, 1, · · · , 1) (see Xu and Shi[52]).

accepted.question_text: For a fixed integer k ≥ 2, let ex(n, C2k) denote the Turán number of the even cycle C2k, meaning the maximum number of edges in an n-vertex graph containing no copy of C2k. Does there exist a positive constant c such that ex(n, C2k) ≥ c n^(1+1/k)?
accepted.context_brief: Lower bounds for even-cycle Turán numbers.

evidence.quote: P. Erdös conjectured that there exists a positive constant c such that ex(n, C2k) ≥ cn1+1/k(see Erdös[11]).

accepted.question_text: Let G be a simple eulerian graph on n vertices, and let cd(G) denote the smallest number of edge-disjoint circuits in a circuit decomposition of G. Must cd(G) ≤ |V(G)|/2 hold for every simple eulerian graph G?

evidence.quote: The following conjecture is due to Hajós(see [36]). Hajós conjecture: cd(G) ≤ |V (G)| / 2
for every simple eulerian graph G.
